task: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling

merged.claim: Parker Conrad is co-founder and CEO of Rippling; he previously co-founded Wikinvest/SigFig and Zenefits (CEO, resigned Feb 2016).
Prasanna Sankar co-founded Rippling in 2016.
Sankar served as Rippling CTO (still co-founder/CTO in a March 2019 interview; current status unconfirmed).
Albert Strasheim is Rippling CTO and SVP Engineering (announced 2024-09-06); previously VP Engineering at Segment and held senior engineering roles at D2iQ and Cloudflare.
Adam Swiecicki is Rippling's CFO.
Adil Syed is Rippling CFO; he joined from Snap, where he was Head of Strategy and Operations and helped lead Snap's IPO.
Matt (Charles Matthew) MacInnis is Rippling's Chief Operating Officer.
Matt MacInnis is Rippling's President/Chief Product Officer (per company About page, 2026-10-21).
Eisar Lipkovitz is Rippling's Chief Product Officer; previously CIO of JPMorgan's Corporate & Investment Bank, EVP and Head of Rideshare at Lyft, and 15 years at Google.
Bridget Abraham is Rippling's Chief Compliance Officer.
Matt Plank is Rippling's Chief Revenue Officer.
Martin White is Rippling's General Counsel.
Stephanie Ho is Rippling's SVP Customer Experience.
Sunil Raman is Rippling's SVP Business and Product Operations.
Chris Campbell announced on 2025-10-31 that he was leaving Rippling after five years as Deputy General Counsel (self-reported).
Wan Agus (formerly CTO at Credit Karma) joined Rippling in December 2025 as SVP of Engineering.
Gang Wang (formerly CTO at Nuvei, with senior engineering roles at Stripe and Intuit) joined Rippling in December 2025 as SVP of Engineering.
In October 2017 Parker Conrad settled SEC charges (fine paid, no admit/deny) over misleading investors about regulatory compliance at Zenefits; not a Rippling action.
Series A: $45M led by Kleiner Perkins (Mamoon Hamid), with Initialized Capital, Threshold Ventures and Y Combinator participating (2019).
Series B: $145M led by Founders Fund (2020).
Series C: $250M (Oct 2021) led by Sequoia Capital Global Equities and Global Growth, with Greenoaks participating; $6.5B valuation per TacticalVC.
Series D: $250M (May 2022) co-led by Bedrock and Kleiner Perkins, with Y Combinator and Sequoia; $11.25B valuation.
Series E: $500M (March 2023) led by Greenoaks, raised within about 12 hours in response to the SVB failure; valuation reported as $11.25B.

Series F (April 2024): $200M primary at $13.5B valuation (Reuters reported Coatue-led), plus a tender/repurchase of up to $590M from employees, former employees and early investors (not primary capital).

Series G (announced 2025-05-09): $450M new financing at $16.8B valuation, plus agreements to repurchase up to $200M of equity from current/former employees; investors include Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator; no lead investor per CNBC/Sacra.
The latest publicly evidenced valuation remains the May 2025 Series G at $16.8B; no later valuation found as of CNBC's May 2026 profile.
Rippling raised a $7M round in 2017 (per Fireround).
Total funding is about $1.85B ($1.847B per Fireround across eight rounds) after Series G.
Rippling's careers page states $1.4B+ raised; needs reconciliation against primary financing documents and tender-offer treatment.

Rippling sells a unified workforce-management cloud platform spanning HR, IT and finance/spend (payroll, benefits, SSO/identity, devices, bill pay, corporate cards, recruiting, AI) on a single employee data set; 20+ products (company claim).
Product ecosystem includes HRIS, benefits, PEO, HR services, headcount planning, recruiting, performance management, LMS, time and attendance, payroll, IT and finance products (company claim).
Business model: per-employee-per-month SaaS subscriptions by module, plus transactional revenue from international payroll FX, card interchange, instant wage transfers and EOR services (Sacra).
Advertised pricing starts at $8 per employee per month plus a monthly base fee (observed 2026-10-21); actual pricing requires a quote.
Rippling claims payroll/workforce support in 185+ countries and 50+ currencies (product-specific coverage).
Rippling offers EOR, global payroll, global contractor payments and contractor-of-record services, with local-currency payroll and global tax filing (company claim).
Rippling is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Ireland (European HQ Dublin), the UK, India (Bengaluru) and Australia (Sydney, first APAC office).
Rippling launched Rippling AI and, in June 2026, Rippling Data Cloud, a business-intelligence product connecting organizational and third-party data.
Rippling had 20,000+ customers as of May 2025 (TechCrunch/Reuters).
Rippling's global page says it is trusted by 25,000+ businesses (company claim).
Rippling claims more than 30,000 customers as of 2026-10-21 (comparison page).
Company-claimed ARR of $175M in 2022.
ARR of about $350M at end of 2023 (The Information via CNBC; company-claimed).
Rippling had about $570M annualized revenue in early 2025 (around 2025-05-09; The Information via TechCrunch; unaudited).
CNBC reported Rippling's ARR crossed $1B in 2025; no audited statements.
Rippling claims $1B+ ARR as of April 2026 (annual revenue around $1B as of July 2026 per TechCrunch interview with Conrad).
Sacra estimates Rippling reached $1B annualized revenue in March 2026, up from $850M at end of 2025 (aggregator estimate).
Parker Conrad said in April 2026 that revenue was growing ~78% YoY, with growth accelerating for three consecutive quarters (company claim, unaudited).
Conrad told CNBC in May 2025 that annual revenue growth was well over 30%.
Rippling's careers page reports 3x year-over-year revenue growth (company claim).
Rippling claims 99.5% PEO customer retention in Fall 2024 renewals; 10+ product lines each exceed $1M ARR, with new products reaching $1M ARR in 5-6 months.
Net revenue retention was approximately 200% as of May 2022 (Contrary Research estimate) vs 110-120% median for enterprise SaaS.
Sigma360 and Rippling announced a partnership in June 2026 for real-time sanctions screening across Rippling's global payments infrastructure.
Named customers Walker Advertising, Morning Consult and Four Hands (company claim).
Chess.com is a named Rippling customer.
Kleiner Perkins is a Rippling customer (also an investor).
Y Combinator became a Rippling customer in early 2025 (also an investor).
Clay is a named Rippling customer.
Cursor and Sierra are named Rippling customers (company claims cited by TechCrunch).
Blank Street Coffee, Barry's and CookUnity are named customers on Rippling's site.
Dude Wipes, NinjaTech AI, The Channel Company and Clariti are named customers in Rippling customer stories.
Sequoia (the benefits adviser, not Sequoia Capital) has a compensation-and-benefits partnership integrating with Rippling HCM and benefits administration.

In March 2025 Rippling (People Center, Inc.) sued Deel and executives in N.D. Cal. (25-cv-02576-CRB) alleging corporate espionage, with RICO, trade-secret misappropriation, tortious interference and unfair competition claims (allegations only; no final merits finding).
Rippling also sued Deel in Ireland in March 2025; Deel countersued and filed an anti-SLAPP motion in Delaware.

A Feb 23, 2026 federal order denied Deel's forum, jurisdiction and service challenges and most dismissal requests (RICO proceeds), but dismissed in part Rippling's state-law claims; core federal claims continue.

On Feb 25, 2026 Judge Breyer issued a 49-page ruling letting Rippling's RICO and trade-secret suit against Deel, its CEO, COO and Board Chair proceed, finding three plausible predicate acts (obstruction, wire fraud, trade secret theft) (company claim).

Sept 25, 2026 order in Rippling-Deel: partly granted/denied dismissal of Deel's counterclaims (against Rippling, Conrad and ex-employee Keith O'Brien), compelled arbitration of the most serious counterclaims, denied motion to strike a central witness's testimony, refused to reopen the earlier ruling, and let some false/comparative-advertising claims survive; docket active with a joint discovery letter filed Oct 19; no final resolution.
In April 2025 the alleged Deel spy (former Rippling employee) admitted in an affidavit in an Irish court to spying for Deel at the CEO's direction (Reuters; Fortune called it a major scandal).
The Feb 2026 order recites allegations that the former employee accessed and transmitted confidential information from Rippling's Salesforce, Slack and Google repositories.
CNBC reports a criminal investigation into Deel (not Rippling).

Red flag: Russia/sanctions-related scrutiny over payments to contractors in Russia, with possible banking-partner implications; appears in contested statements in the Deel litigation, civil not a regulator finding, unverified and regulatory exposure unresolved.
Glassdoor: Rippling rated 3.6/5 from ~1,300 reviews, 66% recommend, 75% positive business outlook; senior management and work-life balance each ~3.0, culture 3.5, career opportunities 3.9.
Glassdoor CEO approval for Parker Conrad is 80%.
Only 34% of Glassdoor reviewers approve of the CEO.
Red flag: Rippling's Glassdoor rating declined 4% over the prior twelve months.

Employee reviews cite workload, burnout, understaffing, low pay relative to workload, high turnover and management concerns (including a June 2026 review; unverified), alongside positives on colleagues, learning and product quality.
Glassdoor: Customer Support employees rate Rippling 3.0/5 (20 reviews), 22% below IT-industry average, with support compensation rated 2.8/5.
Glassdoor: compensation and benefits rated 3.9/5 and stable over 12 months.
Trustpilot shows Rippling at 4.5/5 from 2,576 reviews; positive on usability and onboarding, with complaints about technical issues, slow loading, complex implementation and timesheets.
BBB lists 80 complaints against Rippling over three years (35 closed in the prior 12 months) on cancellation, billing, onboarding and support (no customer-volume denominator).

Red flag: Rippling remains unprofitable (Reuters 2024 and May 2025), choosing growth over profitability and relying on primary financing plus employee-equity buybacks; path to profitability is a key underwriting question.
Rippling said no IPO is imminent; Conrad said it needs to become profitable before going public (CNBC/Reuters, May 2025).
CNBC reported Conrad had avoided layoffs at Rippling.
Unverified Blind posts reference Rippling layoffs around Aug-Sept 2022; no verified numbers.
The March 2023 SVB collapse froze Rippling's funds and briefly halted customer payrolls until ~$500M emergency funding was raised; an operational concentration risk event.
Rippling held about $1B in cash as of 2024 while unprofitable (Reuters via Wikipedia).
Rippling headcount ~2,800 in 2024 (Reuters).
Rippling had more than 4,000 employees as of 2025-05-09 (TechCrunch).
Rippling headcount ~5,000 in 2025 (Latka: 5,000 in Nov 2025, up from 3,630 a year earlier).
Rippling's careers page reports 6,000+ global employees (vs 260 onboarded in 2020); company claim, unaudited.
UnifyGTM shows 7,415 Rippling employee profiles in July 2026 (profile-coverage measure, not company-reported).
Rippling stated it was hiring across all roles at the May 2025 Series G announcement.
Careers page reports $35B of payroll processed, 30,000 employee devices managed and 600+ app integrations (company claim).
Rippling advertises 650+ integrations (company claim).
Rippling says 17 Wavemakers were selected from 75,000+ Rippling admins, each using an average of 13 Rippling products (company claim, Nov 2024).
